grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: Contrast with but and instead
grammarPoints.rule: Use but to join two contrasting ideas in one sentence. Use instead at the end of a second sentence to show a different action or idea.
grammarPoints.pattern: past idea + , but + present idea  |  past idea. different idea + instead

chart.title: Contrast with but and instead

intro_examples.text: Long ago, children walked to school, but today many children ride their bikes.
intro_examples.jp: 昔、子どもたちは学校まで歩いて行きましたが、今では多くの子どもたちは自転車に乗ります。

intro_examples.text: Many years ago, people didn't have TV. They told stories instead.
intro_examples.jp: 何年も前、人々にはテレビがありませんでした。そのかわりに物語を語りました。

rows.example: Long ago, children walked to school, but today many children ride their bikes.
rows.jp: but は2つの対照的な考えを1つの文につなげます。

rows.example: Many years ago, people didn't have TV. They told stories instead.
rows.jp: instead は2つ目の文の終わりに置き、「そのかわりに」という意味を表します。

rows.example: Long ago, people had fireplaces. Today some people have fireplaces, too.
rows.jp: too は違いではなく、同じことを表すときに使います。

chart.note_rule: Use but for contrast inside one sentence. Use instead at the end of the second sentence.
chart.note_exception: Use a comma before but. Use a period before the second sentence with instead.
chart.note_exception_detail: Use too when things are the same: Today some people have fireplaces, too.

grammarPoints.subject: english
grammarPoints.title: Comparatives with more + adjective
grammarPoints.rule: Use more + adjective + than to compare two people, animals, or things when the adjective has two or more syllables and doesn't take -er. Two-syllable adjectives ending in -y, -le, -ow, or -er (like friendly, simple, narrow, clever) still take -er instead.
grammarPoints.pattern: subject + be + more + adjective + than + noun/pronoun  |  subject + be + more + adjective + than + one

chart.title: Comparatives with more + adjective

chart.note_rule: Use more + adjective + than to compare two people, animals, or things when the adjective has two or more syllables.
chart.note_exception: Than + the second thing can be dropped when the comparison is already clear from context.
chart.note_exception_detail: Life was more difficult back then (than it is now). You can also use one instead of repeating the noun: This house is more modern than that one.

table.title: Comparing with more + adjective
notes: Use more + adjective for two-syllable adjectives that don't end in -y, -le, -ow, or -er.
Always use more + adjective for adjectives with three or more syllables.
You can drop than + the noun when it's clear from context, or use one instead of repeating the noun.

explanation.title: more + adjective
explanation.body: Expensive is a long adjective, so use more expensive, never expensiver.

tab3_quiz.jp: expensive は長い形容詞なので more expensive を使います。expensiver という形はありません。

explanation.title: Two-syllable adjective
explanation.body: Modern doesn't end in -y, -le, -ow, or -er, so it takes more, not -er.

tab3_quiz.jp: modern は -y、-le、-ow、-er で終わらない2音節の形容詞なので、-er ではなく more を使います。

explanation.title: more + adjective + than
explanation.body: Use more + adjective + than to compare the two activities.

tab3_quiz.jp: 2つの活動を比べるときは more + 形容詞 + than を使います。

stem: This phone is more old-fashioned than that

explanation.title: Use one, not the noun again
explanation.body: Use one in place of the second noun to avoid repeating it.

tab3_quiz.jp: 2つ目の名詞を繰り返さないように、one を使います。

explanation.title: more + long adjective
explanation.body: Old-fashioned is a long adjective, so use more, not -er.

tab3_quiz.jp: old-fashioned は長い形容詞なので -er ではなく more を使います。

explanation.title: more difficult than
explanation.body: Use more difficult than to compare the two classes.

tab3_quiz.jp: 2つの授業を比べるときは more difficult than を使います。

explanation.title: more beautiful than
explanation.body: Beautiful has three syllables, so it always takes more, never -er.

tab3_quiz.jp: beautiful は3音節なので、常に more を使い、-er は使いません。

answers: Video games are expensiver than board games.
Video games are more expensive than board games.
Video games are most expensive than board games.
Video games are expensive more than board games.

explanation.title: Correct comparative form
explanation.body: Long adjectives use more + adjective + than, not -er endings.

tab3_quiz.jp: 長い形容詞は more + 形容詞 + than の形を使い、-er の形は使いません。

explanation.title: more interesting than
explanation.body: Interesting is a long adjective, so use more interesting than.

tab3_quiz.jp: interesting は長い形容詞なので more interesting than を使います。

tab4_master.jp: 新しい家は古い家より現代的です。

explanation.title: more + adjective
explanation.body: Expensive is a long adjective; use more expensive, not expensiver.

tab4_master.jp: expensive は長い形容詞なので more expensive を使います。
この電話はあの電話より古めかしいです。

explanation.title: more difficult than
explanation.body: Difficult takes more, not -er, since it has three syllables.

tab4_master.jp: difficult は3音節なので more を使い、-er は使いません。
電気の明かりはろうそくより現代的です。

stem: This house is more modern than that

explanation.title: Use one
explanation.body: Use one instead of repeating the noun after than.

tab4_master.jp: than の後で名詞を繰り返さず one を使います。
祖母の服は私の服より古風です。

explanation.title: more difficult
explanation.body: You can drop than + the second thing when it's clear from context.

tab4_master.jp: 比較の対象が明らかなときは than 以下を省略できます。
山は海より美しいです。

explanation.title: more important than
explanation.body: Important is a long adjective, so it always takes more, not -er.

tab4_master.jp: important は長い形容詞なので常に more を使い、-er は使いません。

japanese.title: more + 形容詞を使った比較級
japanese.rule: 2音節以上（-er をつけない）の形容詞で2つのものを比べるときは、more + 形容詞 + than を使います。-y、-le、-ow、-er で終わる2音節の形容詞（friendly、simple、narrow、clever など）は -er をつけます。
japanese.pattern: 主語 + be動詞 + more + 形容詞 + than + 名詞/代名詞　｜　主語 + be動詞 + more + 形容詞 + than + one
